summary:
Form only: plan.md is written, nothing is built yet. Buff limestone masses follow the lidar setbacks (31-storey slab with a crown, a broad flat Music Hall deck with a raised stage house, an 18-storey east end). Continuous piers frame dark window strips, and every flat roof is lit.
It reads as Radio City from the street frontage: a 4-tall marquee wraps the Sixth Ave/50th St corner in a red neon line, alternating RADIO CITY / MUSIC HALL letters, a blue neon line and gold bulbs. A 22-tall blue-and-silver blade sign with stacked red RADIO CITY letters rises from the marquee at the corner; three enamel roundels sit above the 50th St run.
Planned departures from the brief: the lidar's 2-wide strip along Sixth Ave becomes the marquee zone, and the plot 1 frontage wall above the marquee stands 2-3 blocks back from the lot line. Rockefeller block in site orientation: buff-limestone Deco masses with pier/dark-strip facades and flat parapeted setback roofs. The red/blue neon marquee wraps the SW corner and runs on along the Music Hall. The RADIO CITY blade rises at the corner, and roundels sit over the 50th St marquee.

Plot 0 tower shell: Plot 0 tower shell built: 31-storey slab, wings, podia and corner block in smooth_sandstone with piers, strips, friezes and the y28 string course; hand-built decks with parapets and lights; crown with lantern box and mast. Marquee, blade, roundel and glazing openings carved as air.
polish: build.mjs: roof.json step disabled by me because the roof tool cleared the crown, lantern and mast above its detected eave (y105); keep it off
Two iron_trapdoor vent hoods per wing not built
Crown deck gray bands are only approximate
elements.md items 1-4 not ticked (my edit failed)
Podium A south face z3 and the H block have friezes but no window strips

waste.what: Diagnosed that build.mjs's roof.json step cleared the whole crown above its detected eave
waste.cost: 2 extra builds, a render and blockAt probes
waste.tool: runParts should warn when the roof tool clears a part's cells, or make.sh should skip it when plan.md says roofs are hand-built

waste.what: Wrote per-mass deck, frieze and pier-wall tables and opening carves as coordinate lists
waste.cost: about 25 pier_wall faces and 12 carve boxes by hand
waste.tool: a masses-and-faces helper that builds the solid, deck, frieze and pier walls and skips faces covered by neighbours

companions.task: quoins at the corners, sills and lintels over ground-storey openings, plinth steps
floodlights on setback decks and lit-window clusters

summary:
Music Hall shell: P2 Music Hall shell (parts/hall.mjs) is built: H-A, H-B (three tiers), H-C auditorium with its hall deck, 3 skylight strips and 8 vent boxes, H-D stage house with a fly-loft trapdoor row, and the H-E 50th St front over the marquee line.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks; `mcd check` reports 0 floating and 0 unsupported blocks, and the front-left tile shows the hall deck and stage house reading correctly.
Left for later parts: piers, walk strips, H-G canopy, marquee, roundels, windows and stage door. Plan notes and elements.md item 11 are updated.
polish: Piers every 4 on the north (51st St) and 50th St faces were not built: the masses are plain smooth_sandstone, so the pier rhythm is missing.
Hall deck walk strips (light_gray_concrete on a 6-grid) were not built; the deck is one gray_concrete field with sea lanterns.
H-G stage-door canopy (x89..94 z50..52 y6..7) was left to P5's stage_door canopy option; nothing builds it yet.
Ground split: the GROUND map puts ground 1 from about x50, but vocab/layGround and PLOT1_RAISED_FROM use x59; I followed the vocab, so x50..58 may sit 1 block low.
Mass heights follow plan.md's mass table, not the ROOFS table (H-A deck 24 vs 33; H-B 32/33); roof-height map values run about 1 higher than the plan.
Vent boxes: 8 placed at the listed coordinates, though the element says 6.
mcd fit was not run: rooms.json has no rooms, so there was nothing to check.

waste.what: Ground-level choice worked out by hand: each mass had to sit on the sidewalk course (y0, or y1 where raised), and put() refuses to overwrite it, so I split every mass at x=59 and picked bottoms y1/y2 manually.
waste.cost: about 6 reasoning passes and one wrong-plinth attempt on paper before the build ran clean
waste.tool: A build-library helper such as `mass(g, box, {top})` that reads the ground map (or the sidewalk course) and starts each column on the right y, so no part repeats the y0/y1/y2 split.

waste.what: Ordering rules were discovered by reading the helpers: skylight_strip and setback_deck only write into air, so skylights must go before the deck, and the glowstone under each skylight is set by hand into the solid mass.
waste.cost: one re-read of the helper sources and a reordering of the calls
waste.tool: A deck helper that takes skylight and vent cells as data and places them in one pass, with a note in the vocab docs that the helpers are air-only and order matters.

waste.what: Refusals inside helpers are silent: put() returns 0 and the part report counts only the runParts-level refusals, so a helper that skipped cells looks like a success.
waste.cost: no retries, but I could only confirm coverage by eye in the render
waste.tool: Have the vocab helpers return their refused cells (or the caller read `out.refused`) and surface them in parts-report.json, not just the runParts report.

waste.what: Piers and the frieze/parapet rhythm were not built by any helper for a non-office mass; I had no cheap way to write a recess pattern on a limestone face.
waste.cost: skipped, roughly 40 cells per pier column I would have had to place one by one
waste.tool: A `pier_face(g, {face, at, from, to, y0, y1, every})` helper that writes proud or recessed piers on a solid face, without the office-strip glazing that pier_wall adds.

companions.task: Cut the piers every 4 on the north and 50th St faces, and the recessed bays between them, so the limestone reads as the Music Hall's pier rhythm and not a flat box.
Lay the hall deck's light_gray walk strips on the 6-grid and the parapet coping, so the deck reads as a built roof and not a single gray field.
Light the hall deck's skylight glowstone and check the stage-house deck lanterns with `mcd light` once the marquee and windows are in, so no roof cell stays at light 0.

summary:
East end shell: P3 East end shell is in parts/east.mjs: base E-A (deck y18, parapet y19) with the party strip E-B, the west wing E-C, E-E step, E-F/E-G setbacks, the E-D tower (deck 62), the E-H crown, E-I penthouse with four vent boxes, and three roof gardens.
Ground rule applied: masses start at y1 on ground 0 and y2 on the raised ground (x>=127), since layGround fills y0 and the raised y1. The light well, the Plaza forecourt notch and the shopfront storeys (y1..5) are carved for the other parts.
make.sh finished with a whole build.nbt. Part line: 113,496 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. check: 0 floating, 0 orphans after one fix. fit: OK. Aerial render reads as a stepped Rockefeller-style tower.
polish: Elements 2 and 3 (piers, strips, friezes) are built only on the exposed faces of plot 2 masses; the blind faces (E-C west, E-E, returns, E-B) have none, and friezes sit at deck-1 under the deck rather than as a string under each parapet line.
Shopfront bays, the Plaza lobby glazing and the x150 Plaza entrance are left to P5 (facade); I only carved their openings (y1..5 on the 50th/51st St faces, x155, and the Plaza forecourt).

E-H crown has no piers or strips, only the solid limestone mass with its deck; the floodlights and sea-lantern grid on the decks are left to P6 (setback_deck placed only the default lantern grid every 6).
The plan's ground-level Y (y0 masses) is shifted to y1/y2 because the shared ground course occupies y0 (and y1 on raised cells); tops match the plan, the base starts one or two blocks higher.
E-D' returns are solid limestone to y63 with no deck and no roof treatment; the light well is open to the sky at y1..19 but its bottom is y0 paving with no lantern (P6).

waste.what: Worked out which deck/mass sits on which base, where the split at x=126/127 changes the ground course (y1 vs y2), and which cells the light well, Plaza notch and shopfronts remove, cell by cell from the footprint grid.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of reasoning and two rebuilds; the orphan piers at x155 z38..41 came from carving the plaza notch before placing the piers
waste.tool: A base-mass helper that takes an x-range and a ground line (ground course y0, raised cells one higher) and splits itself, plus a `carve` in vocab (it is only exported from the build library, so I imported it by absolute path).

waste.what: Stacked masses (solid to deck-2, frieze at deck-1, deck and parapet at deck) written as three calls per mass, with each exposed face's pier_wall called by hand with over:[smooth_sandstone].
waste.cost: about 20 calls for plot 2; pier_wall silently refuses a solid face without the over list
waste.tool: A `stacked(box, {yb, deck, faces})` vocab helper that carries the limestone, frieze, deck and face piers together, and documents the over requirement for pier_wall.

waste.what: Checked the plan's Plaza and light-well coordinates against the plot 2 footprint grid by reading rows, since they disagree at z14..15 and z38..41.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of row counting
waste.tool: A `mcd plan`-style footprint printer for the kit's grids, or a check that flags plan notches against the footprint.

waste.what: Judged the aerial render by eye for setbacks and piers; no numeric check of the roof rhythm.
waste.cost: 2 renders
waste.tool: `mcd render --view` presets for the Plaza and the 50th St aerial, plus a roof-height census against the ROOF HEIGHT map.

companions.task: Lay the E-A base and the setback walls, the piers and the cut_sandstone friezes, and cut the light well and the Plaza notch with the right plinth courses.
Glaze the shopfront storeys and the Plaza lobby behind the carved openings (y1..5 and x150 z18..35), with the bronze mullions.
Finish the deck and parapet details (E-C 44, E-D 62, E-H 66) and the penthouse vent lids, with the sea-lantern grid.
Plant the roof gardens on the base deck and the west wing deck: moss, the persistent hedge, azaleas, and lanterns on the kerbs.

summary:
Marquees: parts/marquee.mjs builds all marquee runs: plot 0 west (x1 z5..50), the rounded plot 0 corner at x1..2 z51..52, plot 0 south (z52 x3..26), plot 1 south (z52 x41..85), iron end cheeks, and the six RADIO CITY / MUSIC HALL word placements per plan.
make.sh finishes with a whole build.nbt; the Marquees line shows 1179 placed, 0 REFUSED, 0 off-palette. `mcd fit` is OK, and the corner and west/south runs render as intended.
Open: plot 1's marquee is a floating group in `mcd check` until P2 builds H-E (z50..51, y11..25) above it, and 48 soffit sea lanterns are flagged as unsupported attachments.
polish: Plot 1's marquee (x40..86 z51..52 y6..10) is a floating group in `mcd check` until P2 builds H-E (z50..51 y11..25) above it; then it attaches. Re-run check after the Music Hall shell lands.

The 48 soffit sea_lanterns at y5 under the front rows are reported as unsupported attachments by mcd check; they hang under the red glass above, so this is a checker classification, not a real float. Left as is.

The rounded ends are simplified: the south runs end on iron cheeks at x27 (plot 0) and x40/x86 (plot 1), and the west run's north end closes on cheeks at z4, not a true quarter round. The plan's rounded corner at x1 z52 is kept.
The plot 0 south run starts at x3, not x2, because the corner's south cell takes x2 z51..52 (plan says x2..27). Recorded in plan.md's P4 note.

waste.what: Worked out the marquee's coordinates by hand (run start/end cells, the corner's 2x2 overlap with the south run, cheek positions, word centres) and re-derived each helper's depth/inward convention from its source.
waste.cost: about 6 coordinate passes, two wrong on first try (corner overlap at x2 z51..52, end cheeks)
waste.tool: A marquee plan-to-coordinates helper that takes the plan's from..to ranges and emits run/corner/cheek/word calls with the overlaps resolved.

waste.what: Patched marquee_corner's output after the fact: it wrote a soffit light into the tower's corner-block wall (refused by runParts) and a bottom slab where the plan needs a top slab (fit flagged the end rods as floating); I wrote a scratch-grid copy wrapper to fix both.
waste.cost: 3 rebuild-and-check cycles, about 4 minutes
waste.tool: marquee_corner should take a skip set and a slab-type option; runParts' air-included refusal rule should be in the helper docs.

waste.what: Checked the corner and word placements by zoom and front-left tile, then read them by eye; no tool scores whether the letters read as RADIO CITY / MUSIC HALL from the street.
waste.cost: 2 renders, 2 image reads
waste.tool: mcd zoom with --at and a per-word legibility report from bannerWord.

companions.task: Lay out the RADIO CITY and MUSIC HALL letter sizes and spacing on the marquee faces, and say which band carries which colour, so the words read from the street rather than only in the zoom.
Work out the rounded marquee ends and the cheeks at the east end of plot 0's south run and at both ends of plot 1's run, so the curve reads and the cheeks sit flush.
Hang the marquee from the H-E wall above it, or add hidden support columns, so plot 1's run is connected to the structure and stops being a floating group.

summary:
Blade, roundels, glazing: parts/facade.mjs builds the blade sign, plot 1 roundels and stage door, plot 1 doors and windows, plot 2 shopfronts, east doors and the Plaza lobby; make.sh saves a whole build.nbt.
Plot 0's glazing is not placed: runParts refuses every write into the openings P1 carved to air (372 refused writes), so the entrances, shopfronts, tall windows and plot 0 roundels are missing.
Plot 0 roundels and tall windows are commented out on purpose, to avoid orphan rims and jambs.
polish: BLOCKER for the lead: runParts treats air carved by P1 as placed, so every glazing write into a P1 opening is refused (372 writes in the last make.sh). Affected: plot 0 south and west entrance glass, Sixth Ave lobby bays, 51st St shopfronts, court doors on x29, plot 0 tall windows and plot 0 roundel discs. Either runParts lets a later part fill a cell an earlier part carved to air, or P1 leaves the openings unplaced. I did not bypass the lock.
Plot 0 roundels (centres (14,16) and (23,16) z49) and the plot 0 tall windows (x6, x8 z51; x10, 18, 19, 27 z49) are commented out in parts/facade.mjs. Restore them once the lock is settled.

Blade: P1's corner block walls at x2..4 z51 y11..21 are solid, so the blade's replace cells are skipped. The blade's lower ring depends on the marquee (part 4), still unsupported in the current check.
Plot 0 lit lobby backing: the shroomlight cells behind the glass sit in solid P1 wall, so none were placed. The plot 2 fascia at y6 is skipped where the shell is solid.

Plot 1 items (50th St door pairs, tall windows, north windows and doors, the stage canopy) float in the check until hall.mjs and the marquee land. The canopy sea_lantern at 89,6,50 is unsupported for the same reason. Recheck after those parts.
Nothing rendered or checked by eye. Plan checklist P5 is not ticked. Elements 7, 12, 15 and the plot 1 part of 9 are built; 8, 10, 14 and the plot 0 part of 9 are not. Note P5 is added to plan.md.

waste.what: Worked out every opening's coordinates by hand from plan.md's OPENINGS and P1's carve calls, then checked each by trial: make.sh runs and probe scripts to see which cells landed.
waste.cost: about 4 make.sh runs and 3 probe runs, plus reading tower.mjs carve calls by eye
waste.tool: A build report that lists refused writes by cell with the reason (carved air versus solid) and the owning part. parts-report.json keeps only 8 refusedAt entries.

waste.what: Glazing each opening by hand: glazed_front calls for each run plus a local pane() helper for single glass_pane cells.
waste.cost: about 12 calls by hand, plus a local helper
waste.tool: An opening-fill helper that takes a plan.md OPENINGS row (box, face, frame, glass kind) and places the glazing, so the plan is the one source.

waste.what: Orphan rims and jambs placed outside carved cells, found only after check, then removed by hand.
waste.cost: one full make and check cycle
waste.tool: A pre-check that drops a helper as a unit when its main cells are refused (a roundel is a disc with its rim, a tall window is a pane with its jambs).

waste.what: Reading tower.mjs to learn which cells were air, since the report does not say.
waste.cost: one read of tower.mjs
waste.tool: A per-cell owner report (which part last wrote each cell, air or solid) in parts-report.json.

companions.task: Cut the plot 0 wing and corner-block openings (roundel discs, tall-window slots, entrance recesses) as a shell job before glazing, so the glazier fits glass into real holes and the plaque rims have a face to sit on.
Hang the stage door canopy's sea lanterns and place the 50th St lamp posts once the hall and marquee walls exist, so the canopy and street lamps are supported and lit at dusk.

summary:
Lights and grounds: P6 lights and grounds (parts/lights.mjs) builds 446 blocks: floodlights at the crown, stage-house and plot 2 crown feet, kerbed paved courts and alley, and 22 lamp stubs. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes from this part.
The lit office windows (about 25% of strip glass) are not placed. The tower shell's recess air and solid backing are locked, so the shroomlight has nowhere to go; plan.md Notes says what P1/P3 must leave open, and litFace() is ready for it.
The floodlights float until the hall and east parts land, since those decks are still stubs in this copy.
polish: Lit office windows not placed: the tower shell writes air into the recess cell in front of each strip glass cell (locked for later parts) and solid limestone behind the glass. Fix in P1/P3: leave the recess cell in front of each strip glass cell unwritten (plan RESERVED lit-window backing); then call litFace(g, rand, face, planes, along, [ylo, yhi]) in parts/lights.mjs with the plane and range list in its comment. About 254 candidate cells on the tower and east faces.
roof_lights grid not laid by P6; the decks' flush sea lanterns come from setback_deck in P1/P3. Verify every deck is lit (mcd light) once the shells land.
Floodlights at y32 (stage house on the hall deck y31), y63 (plot 2 crown on the tower deck y62) float in this copy because the hall and east shells are stubs. Recheck with mcd check after they land.

Lamp stubs and sidewalks are placed on the walking levels from the ground map (y1, or y2 on raised ground); render the 50th St run after the marquee lands to confirm the stubs clear the marquee soffit.

waste.what: Worked out the strip glass plane and its cell layout by probing the grid cell by cell (air in front, solid behind) to find where lit backing could go.
waste.cost: about 4 probe scripts and 3 rebuilds, with 254 refused writes on the first two attempts
waste.tool: A build-library helper that reports, before writing, which cells are locked air (placed by an earlier part) versus free air, e.g. `g.lockedAir(x,y,z)` or a runParts --dry-run that lists refusals per part without saving.

waste.what: Hand-picked the lamp stub, floodlight and kerb coordinates from the plan's SITE table and ROOFS table, cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 40 coordinate pairs typed by hand, plus one correction after a lamp landed on a shopfront cell (51st St, z0)
waste.tool: A `lamp_stub_run(g, {axis, at, from, to, every, walkY})` helper that takes walking level from the GROUND map and rejects any cell that is not outside the footprint; and a `floodlight_foot(g, box, {deckY, every})` that derives the foot of a wall from the box instead of hand-typed rows.

waste.what: Checked the lamp and floodlight rows against the render by eye (street view tile) rather than a numeric check.
waste.cost: one street tile read, sparse information at street scale
waste.tool: `mcd render --view` with a named aerial camera on the marquee corner, plus `mcd light --y 32` for a deck-level dark-cell count.

companions.task: Set the lit office strip glass: pick about a quarter of the strip cells, put the shroomlight in the recess cell in front of each (or behind, where the shell leaves backing air), and glaze the lit clusters without a full face.

Leave the recess cells in front of the strip glass open in the tower and east shells (the RESERVED lit-window backing), so the lighting trade has somewhere to place its light; also confirm the crown and stage-house deck tops before the floodlights go on them.

summary: inspection: walk ok and fit OK, nothing to fix
